title: rawtiles conformance corpus manifest
description: Machine-readable index of golden and negative fixtures. A consumer iterates fixtures[], opens each pack with the implementation under test, and compares the observed outcome against expected_outcome (plus expected_reject_rule for negatives). The pack_sha256 and hashes_sha256 fields let consumers detect corpus drift independently of running the generators.

spec_version.description: rawtiles spec document version this corpus targets (e.g. "0.1").

manifest_version.description: Manifest schema version. Bump on backward-incompatible field changes.

generated_by.description: Free-form identifier of the tool that produced this manifest (e.g. "rawtiles-conformance generators v1").

name.description: Stem of the fixture filename, e.g. "golden-smallest" or "neg-25-index-offset-296".

path.description: Path to the .rawtiles file, relative to the conformance/ directory.

description.description: One-line human summary of what the fixture exercises.

spec_refs.description: Spec sections this fixture exercises, e.g. ["§ 4.13", "§ 8.6"]. For negatives, includes the § 11 rule via expected_reject_rule, not here.

expected_outcome.description: What a conforming reader MUST do when opening this pack.

pack_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the .rawtiles bytes. Drift sentinel.

hashes_path.description: Path to the sibling .hashes file (§ 14.5). Required for kind = golden.

hashes_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the .hashes bytes. Required for kind = golden.

expected_reject_rule.description: Required for kind = negative. Identifies the § 11 rule this fixture targets.

rule_number.description: The § 11 rule number, e.g. "14a" for rule #14a.

summary.description: One-line restatement of the rule, e.g. "entry offset must be 4-aligned".

derived_from.description: Required for kind = negative. Name of the golden fixture this is mutated from.

mutation.description: Required for kind = negative. One-line description of the byte-level mutation, e.g. "set header[292:296] = 296 (was 292)".
